change.summary: The Commission must set up and maintain an information system by 30 December 2024 to collect due diligence statements. It must provide specific functions for operator registration, statement tracking, and data sharing with customs and authorities.

obligations.text: Register operators and traders in the Union information system.
obligations.quote: registration of operators and traders and their authorised representatives in the Union

obligations.text: Include EORI numbers for operators placing products under customs procedures.
obligations.quote: for operators placing relevant products under the customs procedure ‘release for free circulation’ or ‘export’, the Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number established pursuant to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, shall be included in their registration profile

obligations.text: Register due diligence statements and assign reference numbers.
obligations.quote: registration of due diligence statements including the communication to the operator concerned of a reference number for each due diligence statement submitted through the information system

obligations.text: Register simplified declarations for micro or small primary operators.
obligations.quote: registration of simplified declarations submitted by micro or small primary operators and assignment of a declaration identifier to the operator concerned

obligations.text: Convert data to identify geolocation where possible.
obligations.quote: the conversion of data from relevant systems to identify the geolocation

obligations.text: Register outcomes of checks on due diligence statements.
obligations.quote: registration of the outcome of checks on due diligence statements

obligations.text: Interconnect with customs through the European Single Window Environment.
obligations.quote: interconnection with customs through the European Union Single Window Environment for Customs, in accordance with Article 28

obligations.text: Provide relevant information to support risk-profiling for checks.
obligations.quote: provision of relevant information to support the risk-profiling for the plan of checks referred to in Article 16(5)

obligations.text: Facilitate administrative assistance and cooperation between authorities.
obligations.quote: facilitation of administrative assistance and cooperation between competent authorities, and between competent authorities and the Commission, to exchange information and data

obligations.text: Support communication between authorities and operators for implementation.
obligations.quote: support communication between competent authorities and operators, downstream operators and traders for the purposes of implementation of this Regulation

reasons: The obligations listed are all addressed to the European Commission to build and maintain the Union information system for due diligence statements.
They describe system functions like operator registration, statement tracking, and data sharing with customs — not actions required of individual traders.
Your shop will need to use that system once it exists, but Article 33 itself does not give you any to-dos.
